title: Eastfield Down
briefing: Eastfield's main compressor has failed during a delivery peak. Kelvarin's engineer is four hours away. The chilled store is at 6.5C and rising.
Priya is in a board meeting. The site manager asks you, the risk analyst on call, what to do first.

context.text: Your second contractor is not yet approved for Eastfield, but they can send someone in two hours.

evidence.title: Store status
evidence.body: Chilled store 6.5C, rising about 0.5C an hour (limit 8C). 190 pallets, 30 of them high-value dairy for a retailer with strict penalties.

evidence.title: What's available
evidence.body: A refrigerated trailer on site (holds about 40 pallets). Northgate has space for 60 pallets, 90 minutes away. Kelvarin: 4 hours.

options.label: Load the 30 high-value pallets into the trailer now and start moving the next most perishable stock
options.feedback: Protects the most valuable, most perishable stock inside the 3-hour window.

options.label: Keep doors shut to hold the cold and wait for Kelvarin: moving stock risks breaking the cold chain on the yard
options.feedback: At 0.5C an hour the store breaches about an hour before the engineer arrives.

schedules.description: Eastfield stock passes 8C before the engineer arrives

options.label: Start moving all 190 pallets to Northgate, oldest stock first, so nothing is left in a failing store
options.feedback: Northgate only has room for 60; trying to move everything slows the important loads.

questions.prompt: What control evidence do you start immediately?

options.label: A timed log of store and trailer temperatures and of every pallet moved
options.feedback: The record you'll need for clients, insurers and the root cause.

options.label: Photos of the store display and the trailer loading, attached to the incident record afterwards
options.feedback: Better than nothing, but not an evidence trail.

options.label: Leave the paperwork until the stock is safe: every pair of hands is needed on the move

questions.prompt: What do you put in your first update to Priya?

options.label: Time, store temperature and trend, actions taken, the decision you need from her, and when you will update next
That the failure follows Kelvarin's missed services, so she can raise it with Procurement and the contract owner straight away
options.feedback: Possibly true, but blame can wait; she needs the situation.

options.label: That the team has it in hand and you will report once the stock is safe, so she can stay in her meeting

questions.prompt: What does this event tell you about the Kelvarin risk you assessed earlier?

options.label: The non-performance risk has materialised: re-rate the likelihood and revisit the renewal decision
options.feedback: Incidents are evidence; update the assessment.

options.label: One failure in a hot spell does not change a likelihood rating built on a year of data
options.feedback: A missed service followed by a failure is not just luck.

options.label: The failure is specific to Eastfield's older plant, so the other sites' ratings can stay as they are
options.feedback: Every site depends on the same contractor.

lesson: When something fails, protect what matters most inside the time you have, keep an evidence trail, and update the risk assessment with what happened.

escalation.text: Nobody from risk picked up "Eastfield Down" in time. The executive team handled it alone, late and without a plan, and the damage spread.
